title: Boot hangs inside clear_lut(). Tap the bug.
explain: A uint8_t can hold at most 255, so i < 256 is always true. After 255, i wraps to 0 and the loop never ends. Use a counter type that can reach the limit, like unsigned int or size_t. -Wextra (-Wtype-limits) warns about this compare.

title: 32-bit MCU. If the sensor never answers, wait_ack() sometimes never times out. Tap the bug.
explain: now and start are promoted to int before the subtraction. When the 16-bit counter wraps, now - start is negative, so the check is false. If start is above 60535, the result can never pass 5000, and the loop waits forever. Cast the difference back: (uint16_t)(now - start) > 5000.

title: After start_blink() returns, the LED blinks at a random rate. Tap the bug.
explain: [&] captures period_ms by reference. The callback runs later in the ISR, but period_ms lives on the stack of start_blink() and is gone after it returns. The ISR reads whatever is now in that stack slot. Capture by value: [period_ms] or [=].

pr.title: Cast bytes before shifting in rd_be32
pr.author: senior-fw
pr.body: UBSan reports a signed overflow when the first byte is 0x80 or more.

explain: Good fix. p[0] is promoted to int, not to an unsigned type. If p[0] is 0x80 or more, p[0] << 24 does not fit in a 32-bit int: undefined behavior. On 16-bit int targets like AVR, << 16 and << 8 break too. Casting each byte to uint32_t first makes every shift safe.

pr.title: Remove deprecated volatile (C++20)
pr.author: junior-fw
pr.body: C++20 deprecated volatile, so I removed it to fix the warnings.

explain: C++20 deprecated only some uses of volatile, like ++ or += on a volatile object, and volatile parameters. Reading a volatile register is still fine. Without volatile, the compiler may read *uart_sr once and loop forever. Keep volatile on hardware registers. Fix the warning lines instead.

pr.title: Simplify timeout check
pr.author: junior-fw
pr.body: Plain minus is easier to read. Release builds wrap anyway.

explain: Not the same. In debug builds overflow checks are on, so now - start panics when the tick counter wraps. Release wraps only because overflow-checks is off by default, and a profile can turn it on. wrapping_sub says the wrap is wanted and works in every build. Keep it.

title: Status is OK. What does this print?
explain: The macro becomes two statements. Only led = 0; is inside the if. errors++ always runs, so the output is 1 1. Wrap multi-statement macros in do { ... } while (0), or use a static inline function.

title: C++20. Halve a signed control error two ways. What does this print?
explain: Division rounds toward zero: -7 / 2 is -3. Right shift rounds toward minus infinity: -7 >> 1 is -4. So x >> 1 is not x / 2 for negative x. C++20 defines this shift. In C and older C++, shifting a negative value right is implementation-defined.

title: MCU switches a 12 V relay coil with an NPN transistor. The transistor dies after some weeks. What is missing?
options: A diode across the coil, cathode to +12 V
A 100 nF capacitor on the base
explain: Current in a coil cannot stop at once. When the transistor turns off, the coil makes a high voltage spike on the collector, often above the transistor's Vce limit. A flyback diode across the coil gives the current a path and clamps the spike near 12.7 V. Every relay, motor or solenoid needs one.

title: Driving loads from a GPIO: 5 rules
bullets: Each pin has a max current, and the whole chip has a total limit. Read both in the datasheet.
An LED needs a series resistor: R = (Vcc - Vf) / I.
Motors, relays and buzzers draw too much current. Drive them with a transistor or MOSFET.
Coils (relay, motor, solenoid) need a flyback diode across them.
For a MOSFET, check that RDS(on) is given at your gate voltage (like 3.3 V), not only Vgs(th).
